sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ajay Kumar,Chandrama Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Indra Kumar Singh Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.

By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No. 71 of 2022 at Police Station- Rijor, District- Etah under Sections 498A, 304B, IPC and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
The applicant is in jail since 15.06.2022.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 13.06.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Ajay Kumar and Chandrama Singh, learned counsels on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya,
learned AGA-I and Sri Virendra Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the informant from the record,
entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The applicant is the husband of the deceased.

Shailendra vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184492530/
1
2. The applicant never harassed the deceased nor did he demand dowry.
3. The applicant is bereaved by the death of his wife.
4. The deceased was a sensitive lady, who was prone to extreme reactions even over trivial issues.
5. On the fateful day the deceased took the extreme step of ending her life after petty disagreement over her visit to parental house.
The deceased committed suicide by hanging.

6. The post mortem report opines that:
(i) The cause of death is asphyxia due to antemortem hanging.
(ii) Hyoid bone was found to be intact.
(iii) Ligature marks were consistent with the hanging.
7. The applicant did not abet or instigate the deceased to commit suicide.
8. The viscera report opines that no poison was found in the sample.
9. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
10. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to cooperate with the court proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Shailendra be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

Order Date :- 18.7.2023 Pravin  Shailendra vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184492530/
